19	
20	A single-file `add` registers the file's full SHA-256 digest, byte size and
21	resolved absolute source path, and all three are read from the same stable
22	regular file: the source is checked before and after the read, and the read
23	itself is pinned to the confirmed file. If the source is rewritten, appended
24	to, truncated, deleted and recreated, or replaced by another file (even one
25	with identical content, size and modification time) while it is being
26	confirmed or read — or if the path vanishes, becomes a directory or a
27	symlink, or cannot be opened or read in full — the import fails with the
28	source path and the reason, and no sample is registered. Content that
29	happens to match an existing digest never masks such a failure. A source
30	path that is a symlink when the command starts is still followed and its
31	target imported.
32	
33	## Importing a directory
34	
35	A whole directory of images can be registered in one batch:
36	
37	```bash
38	python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --label cat
39	python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --recursive
40	```
41	
42	(The shorter `import` alias is equivalent.)
43	
44	- Only regular files with an extension of `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.bmp`,
45	  `.gif` or `.webp` (matched case-insensitively) are candidates. Symlinks
46	  and other entry types never qualify; recursion stays on the top level
47	  unless `--recursive` is given and never descends through symlinked
48	  directories. Files that appear after the scan are left for the next
49	  import.
50	- Candidates are ordered by their path relative to the source directory,
51	  with `/` separators, compared by Unicode code point.
52	- Samples are identified by their full SHA-256 digest. When several
53	  candidates share content that the workspace does not yet know, only the
54	  sorted-first candidate is added; the rest report `duplicate`. Digests
55	  already in the workspace always report `duplicate` and keep their
56	  original source, label and revision history — the batch label never
57	  overwrites an existing record.
58	- `--label` applies only to genuinely new samples. Omitting it leaves
59	  them unlabeled; the empty string also means unlabeled; any other string
60	  is kept literally.
61	- The result is JSON: the candidate count, the number added, the number
62	  of duplicates, and every candidate's relative path, full digest and
63	  `added`/`duplicate` status in scan order. Empty directories and
64	  all-duplicate imports succeed with zero added.
65	- The batch is all-or-nothing: a missing or non-directory source, a
66	  directory that cannot be scanned, a candidate that cannot be read in
67	  full, or a candidate whose identity, size or modification time changes
68	  while it is read fails the whole import with the path and reason and
69	  leaves no new samples. The batch commits through the same journal as
70	  single-file imports, so an interruption shows either the old state or
71	  the complete batch, and concurrent label batches are never lost.
72	
73	## Split plans
74	
75	A split plan divides every sample currently in the manifest into a
76	train/validation/test set. Plans are saved under
77	`.vision-workbench/splits/<name>.json` and never change afterwards.
78	
79	```bash
80	python3 -m vision_workbench split create ./workspace baseline \
81	    --seed 42 --train 0.6 --validation 0.2 --test 0.2
82	python3 -m vision_workbench split show ./workspace baseline
83	```
84	
85	- The three ratios must be finite numbers in `[0, 1]` that sum to exactly
86	  one; any of them may be zero. Decimals (`0.1`) and fractions (`1/3`) are
87	  both accepted and handled with exact rational arithmetic.
88	- Stratification guarantees that, for every class and for the dataset as a
89	  whole, each set's count differs from its proportional expectation by
90	  strictly less than one — even for classes with one or two samples.
91	- Assignments depend only on sample content digests, labels and the seed,
92	  so they are stable across import order, manifest ordering, workspace
93	  location and restarts. Samples are listed by digest in each set.
94	- Unlabeled samples (no label or an empty label) form their own stratum,
95	  reported under the empty-string key `""`; a real class literally named
96	  `unlabeled` is kept separate.
97	- Creating under an existing name reuses the plan only when the seed,
98	  ratios, sample identities and labels all match; otherwise it reports a
99	  name conflict and leaves the original untouched. Sample identities and
100	  labels are snapshotted from one complete manifest state, so a batch that
101	  changes several labels is seen wholly before or wholly after the plan,
102	  never half-applied. Concurrent creation of one name is atomic: exactly
103	  one request creates it, identical requests reuse it and differing
104	  requests conflict; plans with different names all save, and a plan is
105	  only ever read whole or reported as not found.
106	
107	## Exporting a split plan
108	
109	A saved split plan can be exported as a portable, offline ZIP package:
110	
111	```bash
112	python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip
113	```

116	  each with the same numbered ImageFolder class directories (`class_01`,
117	  `class_02`, ...), plus a UTF-8 `manifest.json`. Samples are stored as
118	  `<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>`.

120	  assignments and recorded source paths. Later imports, batch label
121	  changes or undos never alter an exported package, and exporting never
122	  writes to the workspace.

125	  labels differing only in case each keep a distinct identity in the
126	  manifest's label-to-directory mapping; no machine-specific absolute
127	  paths are written.
128	- An empty plan exports the three set directories and an empty manifest.
129	- Samples with no label are unlabeled. By default the whole export is
130	  rejected and the offending digest is reported; `--skip-unlabeled` skips
131	  them instead, listing the per-set skip counts in both the result and the
132	  manifest. Skipping never redistributes other samples. A real class
133	  literally named `unlabeled` is exported normally.
134	- Source files are streamed and verified against the saved content digest
135	  while copying: a missing, non-regular, unreadable or changed source
136	  fails the whole export with the sample digest and reason.
137	- `--source-dir` reads sample files from a directory tree instead of the
138	  recorded source paths, which is useful after moving the dataset:
139	  ```bash
140	  python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip \
141	      --source-dir ./moved-dataset
142	  ```
143	  Every regular file under the directory and its subdirectories is
144	  considered (no extension filter, since files may have been renamed);
145	  symlinks and other non-regular entries are skipped and symlinked
146	  directories are never descended. Each exported sample must be matched
147	  to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan — a same-named file with
148	  different content does not qualify. When several files share content,
149	  the one whose `/`-separated relative path sorts first by Unicode code
150	  point is used. Files unrelated to the plan are read (an unreadable file
151	  anywhere fails the export) but never included. The plan still decides
152	  sample identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions;
153	  the lookup is used for this export only and is never written back. A
154	  missing or non-directory source, an unreadable directory or file, or a
155	  sample with no matching content fails the whole export with the path
156	  and reason; the package is byte-identical to a normal export of the
157	  same plan, options and content. For an empty plan (or when every sample
158	  is skipped) the directory only has to exist and be a directory.
159	- The target must not already exist; it is written atomically, so a failure
160	  or interruption leaves no incomplete file. Concurrent exports to the
161	  same path are serialized and at most one succeeds.
162	- Package bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source
163	  content: exporting at a different time, from a copied workspace or to a
164	  different path yields byte-identical ZIPs, and source modification times
165	  do not matter.
166	
167	## Tests
168	
169	```bash
170	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
171	```
172	
173	## Batch label updates
174	
175	Labels of already-imported samples can be changed in batches. A batch is a
176	UTF-8 JSON file:
177	
178	```json
179	{
180	  "batch": "renumber-2026-01",
181	  "changes": [
182	    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "cat", "new": "kitten"},
183	    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "dog", "new": null}
184	  ]
185	}
186	```

188	- `batch` must be a non-empty string.
189	- `old` is the expected current label; `new` is the target label. Both may
190	  be a string or `null`; `null` and the empty string both mean *unlabeled*,
191	  any other string is taken literally (including Chinese text and a class
192	  named `unlabeled`).

194	  digest, a sample listed twice, a non-string/non-null label, a malformed
195	  file, or any sample whose current label differs from its expected old
196	  label rejects the entire batch with the offending record identified.
197	- Records whose target equals the current label are no-ops; if every
198	  record is a no-op, the batch reports `no-changes`, occupies no batch
199	  number and writes no history.
200	
201	```bash
202	python3 -m vision_workbench label ./workspace <digest>      # current label
203	python3 -m vision_workbench batch ./workspace changes.json   # submit a batch
204	python3 -m vision_workbench history ./workspace              # successful batches
205	python3 -m vision_workbench undo ./workspace <batch-number>  # undo a batch
206	```
207	
208	Submitting the same number with the same content again returns the
209	original result without re-modifying anything (list order and the
210	`null`/`""` spelling do not change the content), even if labels were
211	changed in the meantime. The same number with different content is a
212	conflict.
213	
214	`history` lists successful batches in submission order: the samples
215	involved, their before/after labels, and the number of samples actually
216	changed. Failed batches never enter history.
217	
218	`undo` restores the old labels of a batch, but only for samples the batch
219	actually changed and only when none of them was modified afterwards (even
220	if the label was changed back). Other samples' later changes do not block
221	the undo. Undo leaves a queryable record; repeating it reports
222	`already-undone`.
223	
224	Imports, batch writes and undos are crash-safe: a write-ahead journal
225	installs the manifest and the history together, so after an interruption
226	the workspace shows either the old state or the complete new state with
227	its history — labels and their history never straddle the two. Recovery
228	runs under the workspace lock at the start of every operation, so a
229	process that already has the workspace open also completes a peer's
230	prepared transaction without reopening; a sample imported successfully
231	afterwards is never rolled back by that recovery. Concurrent operations
232	are serialized by the lock, so no successful import or batch is lost and
233	two batches modifying the same sample from the same old label cannot both
234	win. Summary, label and history queries each observe one complete state
235	and never report corruption from an in-flight write. Saved split plans are
236	never touched by imports, label changes or undos; plans created afterwards
237	use the current labels, and the same-name reuse/conflict rules still
238	apply.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- No third-party runtime dependencies

## Quick start

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench init ./workspace
python3 -m vision_workbench add ./workspace ./examples/cat.jpg --label cat
```

source path and the reason, and no sample is registered. Content that
happens to match an existing digest never masks such a failure. A source
path that is a symlink when the command starts is still followed and its
target imported.

## Importing a directory


## Tests

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

## Batch label updates

Labels of already-imported samples can be changed in batches. A batch is a
UTF-8 JSON file:

```json
{
  "batch": "renumber-2026-01",
  "changes": [
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "cat", "new": "kitten"},
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "dog", "new": null}

```

- `batch` must be a non-empty string.
- `old` is the expected current label; `new` is the target label. Both may

  digest, a sample listed twice, a non-string/non-null label, a malformed
  file, or any sample whose current label differs from its expected old
  label rejects the entire batch with the offending record identified.
- Records whose target equals the current label are no-ops; if every
  record is a no-op, the batch reports `no-changes`, occupies no batch
  number and writes no history.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench label ./workspace <digest>      # current label
python3 -m vision_workbench batch ./workspace changes.json   # submit a batch
python3 -m vision_workbench history ./workspace              # successful batches
python3 -m vision_workbench undo ./workspace <batch-number>  # undo a batch
```

Submitting the same number with the same content again returns the
original result without re-modifying anything (list order and the
`null`/`""` spelling do not change the content), even if labels were
changed in the meantime. The same number with different content is a
conflict.

`history` lists successful batches in submission order: the samples
involved, their before/after labels, and the number of samples actually
changed. Failed batches never enter history.

`undo` restores the old labels of a batch, but only for samples the batch
actually changed and only when none of them was modified afterwards (even
if the label was changed back). Other samples' later changes do not block
the undo. Undo leaves a queryable record; repeating it reports
`already-undone`.

Imports, batch writes and undos are crash-safe: a write-ahead journal
installs the manifest and the history together, so after an interruption
the workspace shows either the old state or the complete new state with
its history — labels and their history never straddle the two. Recovery
runs under the workspace lock at the start of every operation, so a
process that already has the workspace open also completes a peer's
prepared transaction without reopening; a sample imported successfully
afterwards is never rolled back by that recovery. Concurrent operations
are serialized by the lock, so no successful import or batch is lost and
two batches modifying the same sample from the same old label cannot both
win. Summary, label and history queries each observe one complete state
and never report corruption from an in-flight write. Saved split plans are
never touched by imports, label changes or undos; plans created afterwards
use the current labels, and the same-name reuse/conflict rules still
apply.

1	"""Portable offline export of a saved split plan.
2	
3	An export package is a self-contained ZIP: one directory per set
4	(``train``/``validation``/``test``), each containing the same numbered
5	ImageFolder class directories, plus a UTF-8 JSON manifest.  Samples are
6	stored under ``<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>``.
7	
8	The export is driven solely by the saved plan: its sample identities,
9	labels, set assignments and recorded source paths.  Later imports, label
10	changes or undos never affect an exported package, and exporting never
11	writes to the workspace.
12	
13	When ``source_dir`` is given, files are read from that directory tree
14	instead of the recorded source paths: every regular file under the
15	directory (no extension filter; symlinks and other non-regular entries
16	are skipped and symlinked directories are never descended) is read in
17	full and identified by content digest, and each exported sample is
18	matched to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan.  The new
19	directory only changes where bytes are read from; sample identities,
20	labels, set assignments and package file extensions remain the plan's.
21	The lookup is used for this one export only and is never written back.
22	
23	ZIP bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source content:
24	entry metadata uses fixed values, entries are written in a fixed order and
25	source modification times are never consulted.

67	
68	    Returns a result payload describing the plan, the number of samples
69	    actually exported, the class distribution per set and the per-set skip
70	    counts.  Raises :class:`ExportError` (a ``ValueError``) on any failure;
71	    the target path is never created in that case.
72	
73	    When ``source_dir`` is given, sample bytes are read from that directory
74	    tree instead of the plan's recorded source paths: the directory is
75	    walked (regular files only, no extension filter, never through
76	    symlinks), every regular file is hashed in full, and each exported
77	    sample is matched to a file with the same full SHA-256 digest.  The
78	    plan still decides identities, labels, set assignments and package
79	    file extensions; the lookup is used for this export only.
80	    """
81	    plan = store.get_split(plan_name)
82	    members = _collect_members(plan)

85	    if unlabeled and not skip_unlabeled:
86	        first = min(unlabeled, key=lambda member: member["sha256"])

93	    skipped_counts = {set_name: 0 for set_name in SET_NAMES}
94	    for member in unlabeled:

175	def _build_classes(members: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, str]:

181	    """

192	) -> dict[str, Any]:

194	    for set_name in SET_NAMES:
195	        set_members = [member for member in members if member["set"] == set_name]

227	def _sample_path(member: dict[str, Any], class_directory: str) -> str:

233	def _distributions(members: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
234	    result: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
235	    for set_name in SET_NAMES:

244	# A resolver maps a full SHA-256 digest to the absolute path of the
245	# sorted-first regular file carrying that content, plus the file's
246	# identity (device, inode) captured during the lookup so a swap before
247	# the copy is detected.

251	def _scan_source_directory(root: Path) -> Resolver:
252	    """Walk ``root`` and map every digest to the sorted-first copy.
253	
254	    The directory and all its subdirectories are searched for regular
255	    files only: there is no extension filter, symlinks and other
256	    non-regular entries are skipped, and recursion never descends through
257	    symlinked directories.  Every regular file found is read in full and
258	    identified by its content digest; when several files share content,
259	    the one whose slash-separated path relative to ``root`` sorts first
260	    by Unicode code point owns the digest.  A directory that cannot be
261	    scanned, an entry that cannot be inspected or a file that cannot be
262	    read in full fails the export with the path and reason.
263	    """
264	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]] = {}
265	
266	    def walk(directory: Path) -> None:
267	        try:
268	            entries = list(os.scandir(directory))
269	        except OSError as error:
270	            raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {directory}: {error}") from error
271	        for entry in entries:
272	            try:
273	                is_file = entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)
274	            except OSError as error:
275	                raise ExportError(
276	                    f"cannot inspect entry {entry.path}: {error}"
277	                ) from error
278	            if is_file:
279	                rel = os.path.relpath(entry.path, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
280	                digest, device, inode = _hash_regular_file(Path(entry.path))
281	                current = found.get(digest)
282	                if current is None or rel < current[0]:
283	                    found[digest] = (rel, Path(entry.path), device, inode)
284	            else:
285	                try:
286	                    is_dir = entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
287	                except OSError as error:
288	                    raise ExportError(
289	                        f"cannot inspect entry {entry.path}: {error}"
290	                    ) from error
291	                if is_dir:
292	                    walk(Path(entry.path))

294	    walk(root)

296	        digest: (path, device, inode)
297	        for digest, (_, path, device, inode) in found.items()
298	    }

301	def _hash_regular_file(path: Path) -> tuple[str, int, int]:
302	    """Read one file in full, returning ``(digest, device, inode)``.
303	
304	    The bytes are read with ``O_NOFOLLOW`` so a symlink swapped in after
305	    the lookup cannot redirect the read; any failure raises with the path
306	    and reason.
307	    """
308	    try:
309	        stat_result = os.lstat(path)
310	    except OSError as error:
311	        raise ExportError(f"cannot read source file {path}: {error}") from error
312	    if not stat.S_ISREG(stat_result.st_mode):
313	        raise ExportError(f"cannot read source file {path}: not a regular file")
314	    try:
315	        descriptor = os.open(
316	            path, os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
317	        )
318	    except OSError as error:
319	        raise ExportError(f"cannot read source file {path}: {error}") from error
320	    try:
321	        hasher = hashlib.sha256()
322	        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "rb") as stream:
323	            while True:
324	                chunk = stream.read(_CHUNK_SIZE)
325	                if not chunk:
326	                    break
327	                hasher.update(chunk)
328	    except OSError as error:
329	        raise ExportError(f"cannot read source file {path}: {error}") from error
330	    return hasher.hexdigest(), stat_result.st_dev, stat_result.st_ino

333	def _write_package(
334	    target: Path,
335	    classes: dict[str, str],
336	    members: list[dict[str, Any]],
337	    manifest: dict[str, Any],
338	    resolver: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]] | None = None,
339	) -> None:
340	    """Write the ZIP atomically: lock the target name, stream to a temp file.
341	
342	    The target is never overwritten: an existing target is rejected and a
343	    temp file is used until the whole package has been written and fsynced,
344	    so a failure or interruption leaves no incomplete target.  An flock on
345	    a lock file next to the target serializes concurrent exports to the
346	    same path.
347	    """
348	    target = Path(target)
349	    parent = target.parent
350	    try:
351	        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
352	    except OSError as error:
353	        raise ExportError(f"cannot create target directory {parent}: {error}") from error
354	
355	    lock_path = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.lock")
356	    try:
357	        lock_descriptor = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
358	    except OSError as error:
359	        raise ExportError(f"cannot lock target {target}: {error}") from error
360	
361	    temp_path: Path | None = None
362	    try:
363	        fcntl.flock(lock_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
364	        if os.path.lexists(target):
365	            raise ExportError(f"target already exists: {target}")
366	
367	        fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
368	            prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=parent
369	        )
370	        temp_path = Path(temp_name)
371	        try:
372	            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
373	                _write_zip(stream, classes, members, manifest, resolver)
374	                stream.flush()
375	                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
376	            os.replace(temp_path, target)
377	            temp_path = None
378	            _fsync_directory(parent)
379	        except BaseException:
380	            if temp_path is not None:
381	                temp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
382	            raise
383	    except OSError as error:
384	        raise ExportError(f"cannot write export package: {error}") from error
385	    finally:
386	        try:
387	            fcntl.flock(lock_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
388	        finally:
389	            os.close(lock_descriptor)
390	
391	
392	def _write_zip(
393	    stream: Any,
394	    classes: dict[str, str],
395	    members: list[dict[str, Any]],
396	    manifest: dict[str, Any],
397	    resolver: Resolver | None = None,
398	) -> None:
399	    """Stream the package into ``stream`` without holding media in memory."""
400	    directory_entries = _directory_entries(classes)
401	    file_entries = sorted(
402	        (_sample_path(member, classes[member["label"]]), member)
403	        for member in members
404	    )
405	
406	    with zipfile.ZipFile(stream, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
407	        for name in sorted(directory_entries):
408	            archive.writestr(_directory_info(name), b"")
409	        for arc_name, member in file_entries:
410	            _write_sample(archive, arc_name, member, resolver)
411	        archive.writestr(_file_info("manifest.json"), _manifest_bytes(manifest))
412	
413	
414	def _directory_entries(classes: dict[str, str]) -> set[str]:
415	    entries = {f"{set_name}/" for set_name in SET_NAMES}
416	    for class_directory in classes.values():
417	        for set_name in SET_NAMES:
418	            entries.add(f"{set_name}/{class_directory}/")
419	    return entries
420	
421	
422	def _write_sample(
423	    archive: zipfile.ZipFile,
424	    arc_name: str,
425	    member: dict[str, Any],
426	    resolver: Resolver | None = None,
427	) -> None:
428	    digest = member["sha256"]
429	    if resolver is not None:
430	        # Source-directory export: read from the matched copy only.  The
431	        # plan's recorded source path is deliberately not consulted, so a
432	        # still-usable original location cannot paper over a missing
433	        # match.  The identity captured at lookup time detects a swap
434	        # before the copy starts.
435	        try:
436	            source, expected_device, expected_inode = resolver[digest]
437	        except KeyError:
438	            raise ExportError(

Now let me understand the issue. 

After analyzing the existing code, I've identified a symlink vulnerability in the sample export function. Between the stat check and file opening, attackers can either replace the original file with another regular file of the same content to pass digest verification, or replace it with a symlink to be opened normally, leading to unauthorized file access.

I've clarified the specific security requirements and the optimal solution to fix this vulnerability: use O_NOFOLLOW | O_RDONLY to open the file first, then verify the opened file's attributes to confirm it's the expected regular file, then read from the valid file descriptor.

This solution fixes the TOCTOU vulnerability. I'll check the existing implementation to match the code style, and review existing tests to confirm error message expectations.

    def _read_candidate(
        self, path: Path, rel_path: str
    ) -> tuple[str, Path, str, int]:
        """Read one candidate in full, verifying identity/size/mtime around it.

        Returns ``(rel_path, absolute_path, digest, size)``.  A mismatch or
        read failure raises before the batch is committed.
        """
        digest, size = self._read_stable(path, rel_path)
        return rel_path, path, digest, size

    @staticmethod
    def _read_stable(path: Path, display: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
        """Read one file in full and return ``(digest, size)`` for it.

        The digest and size are guaranteed to describe the same stable
        regular file: the path is lstat()ed before and after the read, the
        open uses ``O_NOFOLLOW`` so a path swapped for a symlink cannot
        redirect the read to another file, and the opened descriptor is
        fstat()ed to prove it is the inode that was confirmed before the
        read.  Any identity, size or modification-time change — in-place
        rewrites, appends, truncation, delete-and-recreate, or replacing
        the path with another file, even one with identical content, size
        and mtime — fails with the path and reason, as do a vanishing
        path, a non-regular file and any open or read error.
        """
        try:
            before = os.lstat(path)
        except OSError as error:
            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
        if not stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode):
            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: not a regular file")
        try:
            # O_NOFOLLOW guarantees the bytes come from the inode just
            # lstat()ed, even if the path is swapped for a symlink meanwhile.
            descriptor = os.open(
                path, os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
            )
        except OSError as error:
            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
        try:
            opened = os.fstat(descriptor)
        except OSError as error:
            os.close(descriptor)
            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
        # The path may have been replaced by another regular file between
        # the lstat() and the open(); the descriptor must belong to the
        # inode that was confirmed, or the bytes read would not come from
        # the file this import agreed to read.
        if (opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino) != (before.st_dev, before.st_ino):
            os.close(descriptor)
            raise ValueError(
                f"file changed during import: {display} "
                "(identity, size or modification time changed)"
            )
        hasher = hashlib.sha256()
        try:
            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "rb") as stream:
                while True:
                    chunk = stream.read(1024 * 1024)
                    if not chunk:
                        break
                    hasher.update(chunk)
        except OSError as error:
            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
        try:
            after = os.lstat(path)
        except OSError as error:
            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
        identity = (before.st_dev, before.st_ino, before.st_size, before.st_mtime_ns)
        if identity != (after.st_dev, after.st_ino, after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns):
            raise ValueError(
                f"file changed during import: {display} "
                "(identity, size or modification time changed)"
            )
        return hasher.hexdigest(), before.st_size

    def summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        self.initialize()
        with self._locked():
            items = self._read()["items"]
        labels = Counter(item["label"] or "unlabeled" for item in items)

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from vision_workbench.exporter import (
    ExportError,
    _scan_source_directory,
    _write_sample,
    export_split,
)
from vision_workbench.store import DatasetStore

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


class SourceDirHarness(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name) / "dataset"
        self.store = DatasetStore(self.root)
        self.store.initialize()
        self._serial = 0

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def add_sample(self, label: str | None, content: bytes | None = None) -> str:
        self._serial += 1
        path = self.root.parent / f"sample-{self._serial}.jpg"
        path.write_bytes(
            content if content is not None else f"content-{self._serial}".encode()
        )
        result = self.store.add(path, label)
        self.assertTrue(result.added)
        return result.digest

    def create_plan(
        self, name: str = "baseline", seed: int = 42, ratios: list[str] | None = None
    ) -> dict:
        result = self.store.create_split(
            name, seed, ratios or ["0.5", "0.25", "0.25"]
        )
        return result.plan

    def export(
        self,
        plan: str = "baseline",
        target: Path | None = None,
        skip_unlabeled: bool = False,
        source_dir: Path | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[dict, Path]:
        target = target or self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        result = export_split(
            self.store,
            plan,
            target,
            skip_unlabeled=skip_unlabeled,
            source_dir=source_dir,
        )
        return result, target

    def run_cli(self, *arguments: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "vision_workbench", *arguments],
            cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            text=True,
            capture_output=True,
            check=False,
        )


class SourceDirExportTest(SourceDirHarness):
    def test_export_from_moved_tree_byte_identical(self) -> None:
        d1 = self.add_sample("cat", b"cat-one")
        d2 = self.add_sample("dog", b"dog-two")
        self.create_plan()
        normal = self.root.parent / "normal.zip"
        self.export(target=normal)

        # Move the files to a new tree with new names and extensions, then
        # delete the originals: the recorded source paths no longer exist.
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "renamed.cat").write_bytes(b"cat-one")
        (moved / "sub").mkdir()
        (moved / "sub" / "dog.unknown").write_bytes(b"dog-two")
        (moved / "junk.txt").write_bytes(b"unrelated")
        for child in self.root.parent.iterdir():
            if child.name.startswith("sample-") and child.suffix == ".jpg":
                child.unlink()

        via_dir = self.root.parent / "via-dir.zip"
        result, target = self.export(target=via_dir, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(normal.read_bytes(), via_dir.read_bytes())
        with zipfile.ZipFile(target) as archive:
            manifest = json.loads(archive.read("manifest.json"))
            by_digest = {s["sha256"]: s["path"] for s in manifest["samples"]}
            self.assertEqual(archive.read(by_digest[d1]), b"cat-one")
            self.assertEqual(archive.read(by_digest[d2]), b"dog-two")

    def test_multiple_copies_uses_sorted_first(self) -> None:
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "b.jpg").write_bytes(b"same")
        (moved / "a.jpg").write_bytes(b"same")
        (moved / "sub").mkdir()
        (moved / "sub" / "c.jpg").write_bytes(b"same")
        resolver = _scan_source_directory(moved)
        digest = hashlib.sha256(b"same").hexdigest()
        self.assertEqual(resolver[digest][0], (moved / "a.jpg").resolve())

    def test_same_name_different_content_not_used(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat", b"real-content")
        self.create_plan()
        # The original source is still in place, but the moved tree only
        # has a same-named file with different content.
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "sample-1.jpg").write_bytes(b"different-content")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
            self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertIn(d, str(caught.exception))
        self.assertIn("no file with matching content", str(caught.exception))
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_unrelated_files_ignored_but_tree_still_fully_read(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "photo").write_bytes(b"abc")  # no extension at all
        (moved / "random1").write_bytes(b"xyz")
        (moved / "sub").mkdir()
        (moved / "sub" / "random2").write_bytes(b"123")
        result, target = self.export(source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 1)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(target) as archive:
            names = [n for n in archive.namelist() if n.endswith(".jpg")]
            self.assertEqual(len(names), 1)
            self.assertEqual(names[0], f"train/class_01/{d}.jpg")
            self.assertEqual(archive.read(names[0]), b"abc")

    def test_unreadable_file_fails_with_path(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "good.jpg").write_bytes(b"abc")
        bad = moved / "unreadable.jpg"
        bad.write_bytes(b"xyz")
        bad.chmod(0o000)
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
            self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertIn(str(bad), str(caught.exception))
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_missing_source_dir_fails(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat")
        self.create_plan()
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
            self.export(target=target, source_dir=self.root.parent / "nope")
        self.assertIn("does not exist", str(caught.exception))
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_source_dir_is_file_fails(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat")
        self.create_plan()
        source = self.root.parent / "afile"
        source.write_bytes(b"x")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
            self.export(target=target, source_dir=source)
        self.assertIn("not a directory", str(caught.exception))
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_symlinks_skipped_and_not_descended(self) -> None:
        d = self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        # Symlink to a file with matching content: skipped, not read.
        (moved / "link.jpg").symlink_to(self.root.parent / "sample-1.jpg")
        # Symlink to a directory holding a matching file: not descended.
        real_dir = self.root.parent / "realdir"
        real_dir.mkdir()
        (real_dir / "deep.jpg").write_bytes(b"abc")
        (moved / "dirlink").symlink_to(real_dir)
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
            self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertIn(d, str(caught.exception))
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_empty_plan_skips_scan_but_still_checks_dir(self) -> None:
        self.create_plan("empty")
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        result, target = self.export("empty", source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 0)
        # A missing directory still fails for an empty plan.
        target2 = self.root.parent / "out2.zip"
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
            self.export("empty", target=target2, source_dir=self.root.parent / "nope")
        self.assertFalse(target2.exists())

    def test_all_skipped_skips_scan(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample(None, b"unlabeled")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()  # deliberately empty
        result, target = self.export(skip_unlabeled=True, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(result["skipped"], {"train": 1, "validation": 0, "test": 0})
        self.assertTrue(target.exists())

    def test_skip_unlabeled_with_source_dir_does_not_need_their_files(self) -> None:
        d_labeled = self.add_sample("cat", b"labeled")
        self.add_sample(None, b"unlabeled")
        self.create_plan(ratios=["1", "0", "0"])
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "cat.dat").write_bytes(b"labeled")
        # No file for the unlabeled sample exists anywhere.
        result, target = self.export(skip_unlabeled=True, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["skipped"], {"train": 1, "validation": 0, "test": 0})
        with zipfile.ZipFile(target) as archive:
            self.assertEqual(archive.read(f"train/class_01/{d_labeled}.jpg"), b"labeled")

    def test_manifest_contains_no_absolute_paths(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "x").write_bytes(b"abc")
        result, target = self.export(source_dir=moved)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(target) as archive:
            blob = archive.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            self.assertNotIn(str(self.root.parent), blob)
            self.assertNotIn(str(moved), blob)
            for name in archive.namelist():
                self.assertFalse(name.startswith("/"))
            manifest = json.loads(blob)
            for sample in manifest["samples"]:
                self.assertFalse(sample["path"].startswith("/"))
                self.assertNotIn(str(moved), sample["path"])

    def test_lookup_not_written_back(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        manifest_before = self.store.manifest_path.read_bytes()
        plan_before = (self.store.splits_directory / "baseline.json").read_bytes()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "x").write_bytes(b"abc")
        self.export(source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.manifest_path.read_bytes(), manifest_before)
        self.assertEqual(
            (self.store.splits_directory / "baseline.json").read_bytes(), plan_before
        )

    def test_failure_preserves_existing_target(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        target.write_bytes(b"existing")
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()  # no matching file
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
            self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(target.read_bytes(), b"existing")

    def test_replaced_file_after_lookup_fails(self) -> None:
        path = self.root.parent / "f.jpg"
        path.write_bytes(b"abc")
        digest = hashlib.sha256(b"abc").hexdigest()
        stat_result = os.lstat(path)
        resolver = {digest: (path, stat_result.st_dev, stat_result.st_ino)}
        # Replace the file after the lookup via rename: a distinct inode
        # at the same path (unlink+create could reuse the inode number).
        replacement = self.root.parent / "replacement.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")
        os.replace(replacement, path)
        member = {
            "sha256": digest,
            "label": "cat",
            "set": "train",
            "source": str(path),
        }
        stream = __import__("io").BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(stream, "w") as archive:
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                _write_sample(archive, "train/class_01/x", member, resolver)
        self.assertIn("replaced after lookup", str(caught.exception))


class SourceDirCliTest(SourceDirHarness):
    def test_cli_source_dir_flag(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "renamed").write_bytes(b"abc")
        target = self.root.parent / "cli.zip"
        result = self.run_cli(
            "export", str(self.root), "baseline", str(target),
            "--source-dir", str(moved),
        )
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        body = json.loads(result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(body["exported"], 1)
        self.assertTrue(target.exists())

    def test_cli_missing_source_dir_fails(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat")
        self.create_plan()
        target = self.root.parent / "cli.zip"
        result = self.run_cli(
            "export", str(self.root), "baseline", str(target),
            "--source-dir", str(self.root.parent / "nope"),
        )
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("source directory", result.stderr)
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_concurrent_exports_same_target_one_succeeds(self) -> None:
        self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        (moved / "x").write_bytes(b"abc")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        cli = [
            sys.executable, "-m", "vision_workbench", "export",
            str(self.root), "baseline", str(target),
            "--source-dir", str(moved),
        ]
        processes = [
            subprocess.Popen(
                cli, cwd=REPO_ROOT, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL
            )
            for _ in range(3)
        ]
        results = [p.wait() for p in processes]
        self.assertEqual(results.count(0), 1, results)
        self.assertTrue(target.exists())
        with zipfile.ZipFile(target) as archive:
            self.assertIn("manifest.json", archive.namelist())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class ResolvedCopySwapTest(SourceDirHarness):
    """The opened copy must be the regular file confirmed at lookup time.

    These tests exercise the gap after the directory lookup has finished
    and the selected copy is about to be opened: the selected path may be
    occupied by a different regular file (even byte-identical) or by a
    symlink before the actual open pins the confirmed inode.
    """

    def _plan_with_one_sample(self) -> tuple[str, Path, Path]:
        digest = self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        selected = moved / "a.jpg"
        selected.write_bytes(b"abc")
        return digest, selected, moved

    def _assert_failed_cleanly(
        self, caught: Exception, digest: str, selected: Path
    ) -> None:
        message = str(caught.exception)
        self.assertIn(digest, message)
        self.assertIn(str(selected), message)
        self.assertIn("replaced after lookup", message)
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_identical_copy_swapped_between_check_and_open_fails(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        # Another same-content copy exists in the tree; it must never be
        # used to paper over the swapped-away selection.
        (moved / "b.jpg").write_bytes(b"abc")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        real_open = os.open
        real_lstat = os.lstat
        replacement = moved / "swap.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")
        state = {"fired": False}

        def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
            if not state["fired"] and Path(os.fspath(path)) == selected:
                state["fired"] = True
                # Distinct inode at the same path, identical content.
                os.replace(replacement, selected)
            return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertTrue(state["fired"])
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)

    def test_symlink_to_original_swapped_between_check_and_open_fails(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        # Keep the confirmed regular file alive as the symlink target: the
        # link resolves to the very inode that was selected, yet the path
        # itself is no longer that regular file.
        original = moved / "original.jpg"
        original.write_bytes(b"abc")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        real_open = os.open
        state = {"fired": False}

        def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
            if not state["fired"] and Path(os.fspath(path)) == selected:
                state["fired"] = True
                selected.unlink()
                selected.symlink_to(original)
            return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertTrue(state["fired"])
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_symlink_at_path_before_open_fails(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        original = moved / "original.jpg"
        original.write_bytes(b"abc")
        # The symlink is already at the selected path when the copy starts.
        selected.unlink()
        selected.symlink_to(original)
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
            self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

            return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertTrue(state["fired"])
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)

    def test_no_fallback_to_recorded_source_after_swap(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()

        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        manifest_before = self.store.manifest_path.read_bytes()
        plan_before = (self.store.splits_directory / "baseline.json").read_bytes()
        replacement = moved / "swap.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")

        def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
            if Path(os.fspath(path)) == selected and selected.stat().st_ino == os.lstat(
                selected

                # Swap only on the first open of the still-original path.

                    pass
            return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

        # Simpler deterministic swap: replace before the copy but after the
        # scan, via a patched lstat that performs the replacement once.
        real_lstat = os.lstat
        state = {"fired": False}

        def racing_lstat(path, *args, **kwargs):
            if (
                not state["fired"]
                and Path(os.fspath(path)) == selected
            ):
                state["fired"] = True
                os.replace(replacement, selected)
            return real_lstat(path, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "lstat", side_effect=racing_lstat):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
                self.export(source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.manifest_path.read_bytes(), manifest_before)
        self.assertEqual(
            (self.store.splits_directory / "baseline.json").read_bytes(), plan_before
        )

    def test_no_swap_export_still_succeeds_byte_identically(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        normal = self.root.parent / "normal.zip"
        self.export(target=normal)
        via_dir = self.root.parent / "via-dir.zip"
        result, target = self.export(target=via_dir, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(normal.read_bytes(), via_dir.read_bytes())

class ResolvedCopySwapTest(SourceDirHarness):
    """The opened copy must be the regular file confirmed at lookup time.

    These tests exercise the gap after the directory lookup has finished
    and the selected copy is about to be opened: the selected path may be
    occupied by a different regular file (even byte-identical) or by a
    symlink before the actual open pins the confirmed inode.
    """

    def _plan_with_one_sample(self) -> tuple[str, Path, Path]:
        digest = self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        selected = moved / "a.jpg"
        selected.write_bytes(b"abc")
        return digest, selected, moved

    def _assert_failed_cleanly(
        self, caught: Exception, digest: str, selected: Path
    ) -> None:
        message = str(caught.exception)
        self.assertIn(digest, message)
        self.assertIn(str(selected), message)
        self.assertIn("replaced after lookup", message)
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_identical_copy_swapped_between_check_and_open_fails(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        # Another same-content copy exists in the tree; it must never be
        # used to paper over the swapped-away selection.
        (moved / "b.jpg").write_bytes(b"abc")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        real_open = os.open
        real_lstat = os.lstat
        replacement = moved / "swap.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")
        state = {"fired": False}

        def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
            if not state["fired"] and Path(os.fspath(path)) == selected:
                state["fired"] = True
                # Distinct inode at the same path, identical content.
                os.replace(replacement, selected)
            return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertTrue(state["fired"])
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)

    def test_symlink_to_original_swapped_between_check_and_open_fails(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        # Keep the confirmed regular file alive as the symlink target: the
        # link resolves to the very inode that was selected, yet the path
        # itself is no longer that regular file.
        original = moved / "original.jpg"
        original.write_bytes(b"abc")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        real_open = os.open
        state = {"fired": False}

        def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
            if not state["fired"] and Path(os.fspath(path)) == selected:
                state["fired"] = True
                selected.unlink()
                selected.symlink_to(original)
            return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertTrue(state["fired"])
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_symlink_at_path_before_open_fails(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        original = moved / "original.jpg"
        original.write_bytes(b"abc")
        # The symlink is already at the selected path when the copy starts.
        selected.unlink()
        selected.symlink_to(original)
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
            self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)

        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_symlink_to_other_same_content_file_fails(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        other = moved / "other.jpg"
        other.write_bytes(b"abc")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        real_open = os.open
        state = {"fired": False}

        def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
            if not state["fired"] and Path(os.fspath(path)) == selected:
                state["fired"] = True
                selected.unlink()
                selected.symlink_to(other)
            return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertTrue(state["fired"])
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)

    def test_no_fallback_to_recorded_source_after_swap(self) -> None:

        with patch.object(exporter_mod, "_scan_source_directory", side_effect=scan_wrapper):

class ResolvedCopySwapTest(SourceDirHarness):
    """The opened copy must be the regular file confirmed at lookup time.

    These tests exercise the gap after the directory lookup has finished
    and the selected copy is about to be opened: the selected path may be
    occupied by a different regular file (even byte-identical) or by a
    symlink before the actual open pins the confirmed inode.
    """

    def _plan_with_one_sample(self) -> tuple[str, Path, Path]:
        digest = self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        moved.mkdir()
        selected = moved / "a.jpg"
        selected.write_bytes(b"abc")
        return digest, selected, moved

    def _assert_failed_cleanly(
        self, caught: Exception, digest: str, selected: Path
    ) -> None:
        message = str(caught.exception)
        self.assertIn(digest, message)
        self.assertIn(str(selected), message)
        self.assertIn("replaced after lookup", message)
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        self.assertFalse(target.exists())

    def test_identical_copy_swapped_between_check_and_open_fails(self) -> None:
        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        # Another same-content copy exists in the tree; it must never be
        # used to paper over the swapped-away selection.
        (moved / "b.jpg").write_bytes(b"abc")
        target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"
        real_open = os.open
        real_lstat = os.lstat
        replacement = moved / "swap.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")
        state = {"fired": False}

        def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
            if not state["fired"] and Path(os.fspath(path)) == selected:
                state["fired"] = True
                # Distinct inode at the same path, identical content.
                os.replace(replacement, selected)
            return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertTrue(state["fired"])
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)

        digest, selected, moved = self._plan_with_one_sample()
        # Keep the confirmed regular file alive as the symlink target: the

            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=target, source_dir=moved)
        self.assertTrue(state["fired"])
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught, digest, selected)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

class ResolvedCopySwapTest(SourceDirHarness):
    """The opened copy must be the regular file confirmed at lookup time.

    These tests exercise the gap after the directory lookup has finished
    and the selected copy is about to be opened: the selected path may be
    occupied by a different regular file (even byte-identical) or by a
    symlink before or while the actual open pins the confirmed inode.
    """

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        super().setUp()
        self.digest = self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        self.moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        self.moved.mkdir()
        self.selected = self.moved / "a.jpg"
        self.selected.write_bytes(b"abc")
        # A second same-content copy sorts after the selection, so it can
        # never become the resolver's choice but is always available as a
        # decoy that must not be used as a fallback.
        self.other = self.moved / "b.jpg"
        self.other.write_bytes(b"abc")
        self.target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"

    @contextmanager
    def _post_scan_race(self, mutate, on_open: bool = False):
        """Run ``mutate`` strictly after the directory lookup finishes.

        With ``on_open`` False the mutation lands before the copy inspects
        the selected path; with it True it lands inside the copy's open,
        after the pre-open lstat has already passed.
        """
        real_scan = exporter_mod._scan_source_directory
        state = {"scan_done": False, "fired": False}

        def scan_wrapper(root):
            resolver = real_scan(root)
            state["scan_done"] = True
            if not on_open:
                state["fired"] = True
                mutate()
            return resolver

        patches = [
            patch.object(exporter_mod, "_scan_source_directory", side_effect=scan_wrapper)
        ]
        if on_open:
            real_open = os.open

            def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
                if (
                    state["scan_done"]
                    and not state["fired"]
                    and Path(os.fspath(path)) == self.selected
                ):
                    state["fired"] = True
                    mutate()
                return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

            patches.append(patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open))
        for patched in patches:
            patched.start()
        try:
            yield state
        finally:
            for patched in patches:
                patched.stop()

    def _assert_failed_cleanly(self, caught: Exception) -> None:
        message = str(caught.exception)
        self.assertIn(self.digest, message)
        self.assertIn(str(self.selected), message)
        self.assertIn("replaced after lookup", message)
        self.assertFalse(self.target.exists())

    def _swap_identical_file(self) -> None:
        replacement = self.moved / "swap.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")
        os.replace(replacement, self.selected)

    def test_identical_copy_replaced_before_open_fails(self) -> None:
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)

    def test_identical_copy_replaced_between_lstat_and_open_fails(self) -> None:
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file, on_open=True):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)

    def test_symlink_before_open_fails_even_pointing_at_original(self) -> None:
        original = self.moved / "original.jpg"
        original.write_bytes(b"abc")

        def make_symlink():
            self.selected.unlink()
            self.selected.symlink_to(original)

        with self._post_scan_race(make_symlink):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_symlink_between_lstat_and_open_fails_even_at_same_inode(self) -> None:
        # The link target is the exact inode the lookup selected; the open
        # must still refuse because the path itself became a symlink.
        def make_symlink():
            holder = self.moved / "holder.jpg"
            os.link(self.selected, holder)  # hard link keeps the inode alive
            self.selected.unlink()
            self.selected.symlink_to(holder)

        with self._post_scan_race(make_symlink, on_open=True):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_symlink_to_other_same_content_copy_fails(self) -> None:
        def make_symlink():
            self.selected.unlink()
            self.selected.symlink_to(self.other)

        with self._post_scan_race(make_symlink, on_open=True):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_no_fallback_to_other_copy_after_swap(self) -> None:
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        # b.jpg still holds the matching content, but it must not be used.
        self.assertFalse(self.target.exists())

    def test_no_fallback_to_recorded_source_after_swap(self) -> None:
        recorded = Path(
            self.store.get_split("baseline")["sets"]["train"]["members"][0]["source"]
        )
        self.assertTrue(recorded.exists())  # the old recorded source still works
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self.assertFalse(self.target.exists())

    def test_failure_leaves_workspace_plan_and_existing_target_untouched(self) -> None:
        manifest_before = self.store.manifest_path.read_bytes()
        plan_before = (self.store.splits_directory / "baseline.json").read_bytes()
        existing = self.root.parent / "existing.zip"
        existing.write_bytes(b"keep-me")
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
                self.export(target=existing, source_dir=self.moved)
        self.assertEqual(existing.read_bytes(), b"keep-me")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.manifest_path.read_bytes(), manifest_before)
        self.assertEqual(
            (self.store.splits_directory / "baseline.json").read_bytes(), plan_before
        )

    def test_swap_after_open_still_reads_confirmed_inode(self) -> None:
        # A replacement landing after the descriptor is open cannot change
        # what is read: the descriptor pins the confirmed inode, so the
        # export succeeds using the originally confirmed file.
        replacement = self.moved / "swap.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")
        real_fstat = os.fstat

        def racing_fstat(descriptor, *args, **kwargs):
            result = real_fstat(descriptor, *args, **kwargs)
            if stat.S_ISREG(result.st_mode) and (result.st_dev, result.st_ino) == (
                os.lstat(self.selected).st_dev,
                os.lstat(self.selected).st_ino,
            ):
                if replacement.exists():
                    os.replace(replacement, self.selected)
            return result

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "fstat", side_effect=racing_fstat):
            result, target = self.export(source_dir=self.moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 1)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(target) as archive:
            names = [n for n in archive.namelist() if n.endswith(".jpg")]
            self.assertEqual(archive.read(names[0]), b"abc")

    def test_no_swap_export_still_succeeds_byte_identically(self) -> None:
        normal = self.root.parent / "normal.zip"
        self.export(target=normal)
        via_dir = self.root.parent / "via-dir.zip"
        result, target = self.export(target=via_dir, source_dir=self.moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(normal.read_bytes(), via_dir.read_bytes())

class ResolvedCopySwapTest(SourceDirHarness):
    """The opened copy must be the regular file confirmed at lookup time.

    These tests exercise the gap after the directory lookup has finished
    and the selected copy is about to be opened: the selected path may be
    occupied by a different regular file (even byte-identical) or by a
    symlink before or while the actual open pins the confirmed inode.
    """

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        super().setUp()
        self.digest = self.add_sample("cat", b"abc")
        self.create_plan()
        self.moved = self.root.parent / "moved"
        self.moved.mkdir()
        self.selected = self.moved / "a.jpg"
        self.selected.write_bytes(b"abc")
        # A second same-content copy sorts after the selection, so it can
        # never become the resolver's choice but is always available as a
        # decoy that must not be used as a fallback.
        self.other = self.moved / "b.jpg"
        self.other.write_bytes(b"abc")
        self.target = self.root.parent / "out.zip"

    @contextmanager
    def _post_scan_race(self, mutate, on_open: bool = False):
        """Run ``mutate`` strictly after the directory lookup finishes.

        With ``on_open`` False the mutation lands before the copy inspects
        the selected path; with it True it lands inside the copy's open,
        after the pre-open lstat has already passed.
        """
        real_scan = exporter_mod._scan_source_directory
        state = {"scan_done": False, "fired": False}

        def scan_wrapper(root):
            resolver = real_scan(root)
            state["scan_done"] = True
            if not on_open:
                state["fired"] = True
                mutate()
            return resolver

        patches = [
            patch.object(exporter_mod, "_scan_source_directory", side_effect=scan_wrapper)
        ]
        if on_open:
            real_open = os.open

            def racing_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs):
                if (
                    state["scan_done"]
                    and not state["fired"]
                    and Path(os.fspath(path)) == self.selected
                ):
                    state["fired"] = True
                    mutate()
                return real_open(path, flags, *args, **kwargs)

            patches.append(patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "open", side_effect=racing_open))
        for patched in patches:
            patched.start()
        try:
            yield state
        finally:
            for patched in patches:
                patched.stop()

    def _assert_failed_cleanly(self, caught: Exception) -> None:
        message = str(caught.exception)
        self.assertIn(self.digest, message)
        self.assertIn(str(self.selected), message)
        self.assertIn("replaced after lookup", message)
        self.assertFalse(self.target.exists())

    def _swap_identical_file(self) -> None:
        replacement = self.moved / "swap.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")
        os.replace(replacement, self.selected)

    def test_identical_copy_replaced_before_open_fails(self) -> None:
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)

    def test_identical_copy_replaced_between_lstat_and_open_fails(self) -> None:
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file, on_open=True):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)

    def test_symlink_before_open_fails_even_pointing_at_original(self) -> None:
        original = self.moved / "original.jpg"
        original.write_bytes(b"abc")

        def make_symlink():
            self.selected.unlink()
            self.selected.symlink_to(original)

        with self._post_scan_race(make_symlink):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_symlink_between_lstat_and_open_fails_even_at_same_inode(self) -> None:
        # The link target is the exact inode the lookup selected; the open
        # must still refuse because the path itself became a symlink.
        def make_symlink():
            holder = self.moved / "holder.jpg"
            os.link(self.selected, holder)  # hard link keeps the inode alive
            self.selected.unlink()
            self.selected.symlink_to(holder)

        with self._post_scan_race(make_symlink, on_open=True):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_symlink_to_other_same_content_copy_fails(self) -> None:
        def make_symlink():
            self.selected.unlink()
            self.selected.symlink_to(self.other)

        with self._post_scan_race(make_symlink, on_open=True):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError) as caught:
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self._assert_failed_cleanly(caught)
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(caught.exception))

    def test_no_fallback_to_other_copy_after_swap(self) -> None:
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        # b.jpg still holds the matching content, but it must not be used.
        self.assertFalse(self.target.exists())

    def test_no_fallback_to_recorded_source_after_swap(self) -> None:
        recorded = Path(
            self.store.get_split("baseline")["sets"]["train"]["members"][0]["source"]
        )
        self.assertTrue(recorded.exists())  # the old recorded source still works
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
                self.export(target=self.target, source_dir=self.moved)
        self.assertFalse(self.target.exists())

    def test_failure_leaves_workspace_plan_and_existing_target_untouched(self) -> None:
        manifest_before = self.store.manifest_path.read_bytes()
        plan_before = (self.store.splits_directory / "baseline.json").read_bytes()
        existing = self.root.parent / "existing.zip"
        existing.write_bytes(b"keep-me")
        with self._post_scan_race(self._swap_identical_file):
            with self.assertRaises(ExportError):
                self.export(target=existing, source_dir=self.moved)
        self.assertEqual(existing.read_bytes(), b"keep-me")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.manifest_path.read_bytes(), manifest_before)
        self.assertEqual(
            (self.store.splits_directory / "baseline.json").read_bytes(), plan_before
        )

    def test_swap_after_open_still_reads_confirmed_inode(self) -> None:
        # A replacement landing after the descriptor is open cannot change
        # what is read: the descriptor pins the confirmed inode, so the
        # export succeeds using the originally confirmed file.
        replacement = self.moved / "swap.jpg"
        replacement.write_bytes(b"abc")
        real_fstat = os.fstat

        def racing_fstat(descriptor, *args, **kwargs):
            result = real_fstat(descriptor, *args, **kwargs)
            if stat.S_ISREG(result.st_mode) and (result.st_dev, result.st_ino) == (
                os.lstat(self.selected).st_dev,
                os.lstat(self.selected).st_ino,
            ):
                if replacement.exists():
                    os.replace(replacement, self.selected)
            return result

        with patch.object(exporter_mod.os, "fstat", side_effect=racing_fstat):
            result, target = self.export(source_dir=self.moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 1)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(target) as archive:
            names = [n for n in archive.namelist() if n.endswith(".jpg")]
            self.assertEqual(archive.read(names[0]), b"abc")

    def test_no_swap_export_still_succeeds_byte_identically(self) -> None:
        normal = self.root.parent / "normal.zip"
        self.export(target=normal)
        via_dir = self.root.parent / "via-dir.zip"
        result, target = self.export(target=via_dir, source_dir=self.moved)
        self.assertEqual(result["exported"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(normal.read_bytes(), via_dir.read_bytes())

content.text:
Done. Summary of the fix:

## Problem
In `vision_workbench/exporter.py`, a `--source-dir` export located each sample by full SHA-256 and checked the selected path's device/inode **before** copying, but the actual read used `source.open("rb")` after that check. Two windows remained:

1. **After the check, before the open** — the path could be renamed over by a different regular file with *identical content, size and mtime*. The post-copy digest check then passed, so the export "succeeded" while reading a file that was never the confirmed copy.
2. The check used `os.stat` and the open followed symlinks, so a **symlink swapped onto the path** (even one resolving to the original inode) passed — the path was no longer the selected regular file, yet copying continued.

## Fix (`vision_workbench/exporter.py`)
Added `_open_resolved_source()`, mirroring the pinning pattern already proven in `store._read_stable`:

- `os.lstat` (no follow) → reject if the path is now a **symlink** or non-regular, and verify device/inode still matches the lookup-confirmed identity.
- `os.open(..., O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW)` → a symlink landing after the lstat makes the open fail with `ELOOP`, reported as a replacement.
- `os.fstat` **on the opened descriptor** → proves the object actually read is the confirmed regular inode. This closes the lstat→open gap that a digest check alone cannot detect.

Every failure message includes the **full sample digest, selected source path, and concrete reason**; it raises the existing `ExportError` (CLI prints `error: …`, exits 1), propagates through the existing atomic writer (temp file removed, existing target untouched, no partial ZIP), and never substitutes another same-content copy or the recorded source path. The non-`--source-dir` path is unchanged, scan-time symlink skipping is unchanged, and ZIP bytes remain deterministic (verified byte-identical in a test).

## Tests
Added 10 tests in `ResolvedCopySwapTest` covering pre-open and tight lstat→open identical-file replacement, symlink swaps (to original inode / hard-linked holder / other same-content copy), no-fallback to the other copy or recorded source, clean failure with existing-target and workspace/plan preservation, descriptor-pinning after open, and unchanged byte-identical success. Against the **unfixed** code, 4 of these fail with exports wrongly succeeding; with the fix all 165 tests pass (155 pre-existing + 10 new).

README's `--source-dir` section and the module docstring now document the pinning guarantee.
